items.claim: The stated tier-1 onset ground misdescribes the grammatical person of the opening verb, and the phrase the row says is named twice is not the same phrase at byte tier.
items.evidence: The onset verse opens with a first-person SINGULAR verb form, אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7-Isa.63.7, byte tier), matched by the row's own rendering “I will tell of the loving kindnesses of Yahweh” (web:Isa.63.7-Isa.63.7); the plural appears only later in the same verse as an object suffix, גְּמָלָ֖נוּ (oshb:Isa.63.7-Isa.63.7, byte tier). So 'a fresh first-person-plural speaker' is byte-false at the onset, and grammatical person does not in fact shift at the front seam at all: the preceding warrior speech is also first-person singular, וְאָב֤וּס (oshb:Isa.63.6-Isa.63.6, byte tier), rendered “I trod down the peoples in my anger” (web:Isa.63.6-Isa.63.6). What the bytes DO support is the self-announcing speech-act verb itself, which is the usable onset signal; the person label is not. Second, the twice-named phrase is ר֣וּחַ קָדְשׁ֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.63.10-Isa.63.10, byte tier) against ר֥וּחַ קָדְשֽׁוֹ (oshb:Isa.63.11-Isa.63.11, byte tier): re-collation makes each splice byte-true at its own verse, but the two runs differ from one another at BYTE tier and at accent-stripped tier, agreeing only at skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) - so the recurrence claim carries no tier label of its own, and both splices also cut away the אֶת (oshb:Isa.63.10-Isa.63.10 and oshb:Isa.63.11-Isa.63.11, byte tier) that governs each occurrence. Third, a glory-catchword hooks across the row's own back seam - תִּפְאָֽרֶת (oshb:Isa.63.14-Isa.63.14, byte tier) into וְתִפְאַרְתֶּ֑ךָ (oshb:Isa.63.15-Isa.63.15, byte tier), with תִּפְאַרְתּ֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.63.12-Isa.63.12, byte tier) already inside the span (sweep: 17 verses book-wide, skeleton tier; 4 of them in this lament) - undisclosed at byte level, though the row does disclose the surrounding material as one liturgical complex. Verified clean and not challenged: the front-seam SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.63.6-Isa.63.6, the ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.63.9-Isa.63.9, and all three paseq sites (oshb:Isa.63.7-Isa.63.7, oshb:Isa.63.9-Isa.63.9, oshb:Isa.63.11-Isa.63.11) are inventory-true and exhaust the span's disclosure layer (sweep: 0 parashah marks, 3 paseq segs, 1 ketiv/qere note over the span's 8 MT verses).

items.claim: The imperative onset is verse-initial in the bytes, both halves of the split verse re-collate byte-true and are assigned to the correct WEB halves, and the theophany echo the row hedges as near-verbatim is byte-identical exactly where the row implies.
items.evidence: הַבֵּ֤ט מִשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ (oshb:Isa.63.15-Isa.63.15, byte tier) is verse-initial in the MT bytes and both witnesses render an imperative (“Look down from heaven, and see”, web:Isa.63.15-Isa.63.15), so the addressee-and-mode onset stands on the original, not on the rendering. The split verse is handled exactly right: לֹֽא נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ re-collates byte-true and is placed at oshb:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19 (FIRST half, the never-ruled clause), and מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ re-collates byte-true and is placed at oshb:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.64.1-Isa.64.1 (SECOND half, the tear-the-heavens clause) - each content claim names its half, and the refusal to cut between the halves is correct because they are one verse's bytes. The device-note echo is byte-confirmed and correctly hedged: מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ is BYTE-IDENTICAL at oshb:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19 (second half = web:Isa.64.1-Isa.64.1) and at oshb:Isa.64.2-Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3-Isa.64.3 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, byte tier), while the verb immediately before it differs, יָרַ֔דְתָּ (oshb:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.64.1-Isa.64.1, second half; byte tier) against יָרַ֕דְתָּ (oshb:Isa.64.2-Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3-Isa.64.3, byte tier) - so 'near-verbatim' is the honest word and both sites sit inside this row's own span. The unit's closing affirmation is byte-true at oshb:Isa.64.3-Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4-Isa.64.4. Residual, not blocking: a restraint-root bracket straddles the row's back seam - הִתְאַפָּֽקוּ closes oshb:Isa.63.15-Isa.63.15, this row's onset verse, and תִתְאַפַּ֖ק stands at oshb:Isa.64.11-Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12-Isa.64.12, immediately beyond the row's back seam (sweep: 3 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) - a bracket over the two rows that neither names, though this row's rival disclosure of the one-complex reading covers the continuity at unit level. The span owes no disclosure at all (sweep: 0 parashah marks, 0 paseq segs, 0 ketiv/qere notes over its 8 MT verses). No mark, crosswalk or quote defect found, and the referent of the addressed 'you' is left undecided.

items.claim: The rejection of the rival onset rests on a connector that exists only in the English rendering, and the row's own claimed onset marker sits mid-verse behind material that continues the preceding affirmation.
items.evidence: The mandated rival is rejected on the ground that the earlier verse is 'introduced by (for), continuing the praise' - but that verse opens וּמֵעוֹלָ֥ם (oshb:Isa.64.3-Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4-Isa.64.4, byte tier), a plain waw-conjunction with no causal particle anywhere in the verse; the causal word is a rendering choice visible only in “For from of old men have not heard” (web:Isa.64.4-Isa.64.4 = oshb:Isa.64.3-Isa.64.3). The load-bearing ground of the rival rejection therefore works in the translation and not in the Hebrew, which is the one place a boundary argument is not allowed to live (a genuine verse-initial causal particle does stand nearby, at oshb:Isa.65.17-Isa.65.17). Second, the claimed self-accusation onset הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א re-collates byte-true at oshb:Isa.64.4-Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5-Isa.64.5, but it stands at token 8 of that verse's 14 and falls after the verse's main caesura; the row's actual front seam lands on פָּגַ֤עְתָּ אֶת שָׂשׂ֙ וְעֹ֣שֵׂה צֶ֔דֶק (oshb:Isa.64.4-Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5-Isa.64.5, byte tier), which is still second-person praise continuous with the preceding affirmation and is rendered “You meet him who rejoices and does righteousness” (web:Isa.64.5-Isa.64.5 = oshb:Isa.64.4-Isa.64.4). A mid-verse rhetorical turn is being presented as a verse-boundary signal, and the mismatch is not disclosed - which also means the rival the row does reject is not the only live rival. Verified clean and not challenged: the crosswalk arithmetic of every dual in this row lands on the right MT verse in the bytes, and the closing SAMEKH claim at oshb:Isa.64.11-Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12-Isa.64.12 is inventory-true and is the span's sole disclosure object (sweep: 1 parashah mark, 0 paseq segs, 0 ketiv/qere notes over the span's 8 MT verses).

items.claim: A recurrence labelled byte-true shares no byte-identical material beyond the negative particle and is quoted in English only, and the frame form the back seam leans on sits mid-verse rather than closing anything.
items.evidence: The rival calls the naming-denial pairing 'a byte-true lexical echo' straddling the front seam. The bytes give לֹֽא נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ (oshb:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19, FIRST half of the split verse; byte tier) against לֹֽא קֹרָ֥א בִשְׁמִֽי (oshb:Isa.65.1-Isa.65.1, byte tier). The verbal forms differ by a prefixed nun and by their pointing, and the naming element differs (a suffixed noun against preposition-plus-suffix), so the longest byte-identical run the two clauses share is the negative particle לֹֽא (oshb:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19-Isa.63.19, first half, and oshb:Isa.65.1-Isa.65.1; byte tier) alone, and at consonantal tier nothing longer than the three-letter root is shared. The echo is real at root level and worth disclosing; 'byte-true' is a tier mislabel on a recurrence claim, and the claim quotes no Hebrew at all, so nothing in the row lets a reader check it. Second, the back seam is argued from a 'closing divine-speech signature': אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה re-collates byte-true at oshb:Isa.65.7-Isa.65.7, but it stands at token 5 of that verse's 19, embedded immediately before the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִטְּרוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.65.7-Isa.65.7, byte tier) - an intra-sentential attribution, not a unit-closing signature; the chapter's only verse-final instance of that formula is at oshb:Isa.65.25-Isa.65.25 (sweep: 1 verse chapter-wide in verse-final position, byte tier). The seam itself survives on the frame onset at oshb:Isa.65.8-Isa.65.8 and on the mark layer; the frame-ROLE claim does not. Verified clean and not challenged: the ketiv/qere notes at oshb:Isa.65.4-Isa.65.4 and oshb:Isa.65.7-Isa.65.7 are inventory-true and the doubled tokens are visible in the bytes (ופרק וּמְרַ֥ק and על אֶל); the bracketing SAMEKH marks at oshb:Isa.64.11-Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12-Isa.64.12 and oshb:Isa.65.7-Isa.65.7 are inventory-true; the split-verse ref carries a valid half-naming dual; and the row correctly holds the identity of the addressed nation rather than deciding it.

items.claim: The row's own quoted onset run begins with a causal connector and repeats a byte-identical noun from the preceding verse, yet is argued as a subject-and-register shift, while the unit's one genuine closing frame form is left unquoted under a tier-3 mark.
items.evidence: The onset splice הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה re-collates byte-true at oshb:Isa.65.17-Isa.65.17 and is verse-initial - but the row's own quoted run opens on the connector כִּֽי (oshb:Isa.65.17-Isa.65.17, byte tier), which subordinates this verse to what precedes, and the noun הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת later in that same verse is BYTE-IDENTICAL to הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת at oshb:Isa.65.16-Isa.65.16 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide at byte tier for that pointed form). Both facts argue continuity across the front seam and neither is disclosed; 'front-seam unmarked' is inventory-true for the parashah layer, but the seam is not unmarked in the letter bytes, and an absence in a tier-3 single-witness layer cannot stand in for the tier-1 evidence that is actually there. Second, the close leans on a tier-3 SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.65.25-Isa.65.25 while leaving unquoted the verse-final divine-speech signature standing in that very verse, אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.65.25-Isa.65.25, byte tier) - the chapter's only verse-final instance of the formula (sweep: 1 verse chapter-wide), a tier-1 signal strong enough to carry the close on its own; the row's WEB quotation stops at the comma immediately before it, while the folded text continues past “in all my holy mountain,” to a closing attribution (web:Isa.65.25-Isa.65.25). The frame at oshb:Isa.66.1-Isa.66.1 that the row cites is likewise byte-true and verse-initial, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.66.1-Isa.66.1, byte tier), but is argued only from the English. Third, the rival rejection rests on 'the same first-person creation verb' resuming: the creating form itself is unchanged across הִנְנִ֥י בוֹרֵ֛א (oshb:Isa.65.17-Isa.65.17), אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֣י בוֹרֵ֑א and כִּי֩ הִנְנִ֨י בוֹרֵ֧א (oshb:Isa.65.18-Isa.65.18) with the person supplied each time by an attached or independent pronoun, and the runs are skeleton-identical, not byte-identical - so both the form label and the recurrence tier overstate the bytes. The span's disclosure layer is otherwise inventory-true and complete (sweep: 1 parashah mark, 0 paseq segs, 0 ketiv/qere notes over its 9 MT verses).
